title: No Driver's License, Full Self-Driving Enabled
message: Enterprise organizations are rushing toward autonomous agents before they have taught employees how to use, verify, and safely supervise AI systems.
analogy_focus: AI enablement and literacy as driver's education; human oversight as the ability to take the wheel.

title: Keys Assigned, Nobody Driving
message: Assigning AI licenses is not the same as adoption, enablement, or business value.
analogy_focus: AI-tool licenses as key fobs or access badges; adoption requires driver training, useful destinations, and workflow fit.

title: Waiting for the Cybertruck
message: Useful everyday AI assistants are already available, but organizations often ignore practical value while chasing more glamorous agentic systems.
analogy_focus: Everyday AI assistants as practical sedans; coding agents and agentic systems as flashy autonomous work vehicles.

title: The Entire AI Highway Department
message: Enterprise AI ambition often outruns the operating capacity required to make it safe, scalable, and real.
analogy_focus: AI strategy as a four-lane highway system; the flawed operating model assigns one engineer to be the fleet owner, traffic regulator, bridge inspector, and first-app test driver.

title: The Guardrails Were The Road
message: The approved AI route with security checks and guardrails may look slower, but it is the route that can actually reach production safely.
analogy_focus: Security requirements as vehicle inspections, road guardrails, restricted-data signs, monitoring cameras, and trip logs; unreviewed shortcuts look faster until the wheels come off.

title: The Strategic Two-Block Commute
message: Premium model access without judgment, enablement, model tiering, usage norms, cost controls, and monitoring turns enterprise strategy into fuel credits.
analogy_focus: Advanced models as Formula 1 cars; everyday assistants as practical sedans; lingering sessions and token consumption as fuel and tire burn.

title: Misalignment Scales Traffic
message: AI use cases scale only when the right driver has the right vehicle, permission to use the route, and enough road capacity to keep moving.
analogy_focus: Capability as skilled drivers, access as keys and route permission, and capacity as lanes, bridges, support, and delivery bandwidth.

title: Same Problem, Better Engines
message: Local AI software creation succeeds while enterprise coordination infrastructure lags behind, repeating spreadsheet-era fragmentation.
analogy_focus: A Data Governance guide clarifies competing client-dataset landmarks; independently working app vehicles later queue and jam at shared intersections.

title: The Pit Crew Becomes Roadside Assistance
message: Expert technical teams need clear work routing so local prototype support does not displace strategic decision systems.
analogy_focus: Data Science as a pit crew; product orchestration routes support to the appropriate service lane.
